md_name: TEM Immunogold Plant Cell Localization Workflow
md_description: This DAG represents a transmission electron microscopy workflow for genetically modified plant cells expressing tagged proteins of interest. It includes plant material collection, tissue fixation, embedding, ultrathin sectioning, immunogold labeling, TEM image acquisition, and downstream digital processing to quantify protein localization within subcellular compartments. The workflow captures key specimen preparation details, imaging settings, and image resolution parameters relevant to studying photosynthetic efficiency and stress-response-associated proteins.

plant_line_gm.reasoning: For the genetically modified plant line entity, I included only intrinsic identity, genetic construct, origin, and phenotype fields because this node describes what the biological source material is, not how it was collected, fixed, imaged, or analyzed. I excluded tissue sampling, fixation, embedding, sectioning, immunolabeling, TEM settings, file properties, and downstream quantification because those belong to later process/capture/signal/derivative nodes. I also avoided any sample-collection identifiers that would be repeated downstream. The fields reflect the experiment’s focus on transgenic lines expressing tagged proteins involved in photosynthetic efficiency and stress response, plus the need to track plant background and observable phenotype.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the genetically modified plant line used as the biological source material; use a stable study-specific code such as PLANT_01. Generated once at the entity level and reused as a parent reference only if needed downstream.
Taxonomic identity of the plant line at the species level; record the accepted species name for the transgenic background, for example Arabidopsis thaliana or Nicotiana benthamiana.
Genetic background or ecotype of the plant line before transgene introduction; record the parental line name or accession, such as Col-0 or WT background designation.

Name of the protein of interest expressed in the genetically modified line, including the tag if applicable; record the full target name used for immunogold localization, for example Rubisco activase-HA or PsbO-GFP.
Molecular tag fused to the protein of interest for detection by immunogold labeling; record the tag identity used in the construct, such as HA, FLAG, MYC, GFP, or TAP.
Status of the introduced construct in the plant line; indicates whether the line is confirmed as stable, segregating, homozygous, or hemizygous at the time material was collected.

Observed phenotype of the genetically modified line relevant to the study, such as altered photosynthetic efficiency, chlorosis, growth defect, or stress tolerance phenotype; describe the observable trait at the plant level before tissue collection.
Whether the line was selected or characterized for a stress-response-related trait relevant to the experiment; use this to note the phenotype category under investigation at the organism level.

Origin of the plant material, such as greenhouse, growth chamber, field, or tissue culture source; record the growth source from which the biologically material line was maintained before tissue collection.

Developmental stage of the plant line when the biological source material was harvested, such as seedling, rosette, vegetative, or flowering; record the stage at the organism level, not the sampled tissue stage.

Free-text description of any additional construct features relevant to the plant line, such as promoter used, selectable marker, or confirmation method, when needed to interpret the tagged protein expression.

tissue_collection.reasoning: For the tissue_collection process, I included only collection-operation fields that describe how plant tissue was harvested from the genetically modified line before downstream fixation. I excluded intrinsic plant-line properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded fixation, embedding, sectioning, labeling, imaging, and file/output details because those belong to later nodes. The fields are limited to collection timing, tissue type, harvesting conditions, and immediate handling needed to reproduce the sampling step.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the tissue collection event; use a study-specific code such as COL_001 to link this harvest to the downstream specimen derived from it.
Plant tissue type harvested from the genetically modified line for TEM preparation; record the anatomical tissue actually excised, such as leaf, root, stem, or cotyledon.
How the tissue was removed from the plant at the sampling point; describe whether the tissue was excised manually, dissected, or otherwise harvested for immediate microscopy preparation.

Time of day when the tissue was harvested, if controlled or relevant to the experiment; record in 24-hour local time, for example 09:30 or 14:15, because circadian status can affect plant ultrastructure.

Elapsed time in minutes between tissue excision and transfer to fixation; measure immediately after collection and record typical values in the range of 0 to 60 minutes depending on handling workflow.
Temperature in degrees Celsius during and immediately after harvest handling before fixation; record the approximate ambient or chilled handling temperature, typically 0 to 25 C.
Free-text notes on any handling details at collection, such as rinsing, trimming, light exposure, or transport conditions before fixation.

leaf_tissue_sample.reasoning: For the leaf_tissue_sample entity, I included only intrinsic specimen attributes that describe the excised tissue itself after collection and before fixation. I excluded collection procedure details because those belong to the upstream tissue_collection process, and I excluded fixation, embedding, sectioning, imaging, and analysis fields because they belong to downstream nodes. The fields focus on specimen identity, morphology, freshness/state, and any observable condition needed to interpret subsequent ultrastructural preparation.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the excised leaf tissue specimen; use a stable code such as SAMPLE_001 so downstream preparation steps can reference the same physical sample.
Anatomical region of the plant from which the excised tissue was taken; record the region relevant to the sample, such as mature leaf blade, young leaf, vein, or petiole.
Immediate condition of the excised tissue at the time it became the sample; describe whether the tissue appeared healthy, stressed, damaged, wilted, or otherwise altered before fixation.
Physical state of the sample prior to fixation, indicating whether it was freshly excised and promptly processed or held briefly before preservation; use to interpret preservation quality.
Approximate linear size of the excised tissue specimen in millimeters at the time of collection; record the major dimension of the leaf piece, typically within 1 to 20 mm for TEM preparation.
Observable surface features of the excised tissue relevant to downstream microscopy, such as intact cuticle, tears, lesions, or contamination; describe the specimen as received for fixation.
Elapsed time in minutes from excision of the tissue to the beginning of the next preparation step; record the actual interval observed for this sample, typically 0 to 120 minutes.

chemical_fixation.reasoning: For the chemical_fixation process, I included only fixation protocol parameters and immediate fixation quality indicators because this node owns how the sample was preserved before embedding. I excluded specimen identity and tissue condition fields because those belong to the upstream sample entity, and I excluded dehydration, embedding, sectioning, labeling, imaging, and signal/output properties because those belong to downstream nodes. I also avoided repeating generic collection metadata already generated for earlier nodes. The resulting fields capture the fixative chemistry, timing, temperature, and practical indicators needed to reproduce ultrastructural preservation in TEM preparation.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the fixation event applied to the excised tissue; use a stable code such as FIX_001 to connect this protocol instance to the resulting fixed tissue specimen.
Primary fixative used to preserve ultrastructure before TEM processing; record the reagent name applied at the start of fixation, such as glutaraldehyde or paraformaldehyde.

Concentration of the primary fixative in percent at the time of tissue immersion; record the working solution concentration used for fixation, typically in the range of 0.1 to 10 percent depending on reagent.
Buffer used to prepare or carry the fixative solution during tissue fixation; record the buffer identity, such as phosphate buffer or cacodylate buffer.
pH of the fixation buffer measured at the time the fixative solution was prepared or used; record the actual pH, typically within 6.5 to 8.0 for TEM tissue fixation.

Temperature in degrees Celsius during fixation; record the temperature at which the tissue was held in fixative, commonly 4 C or room temperature, because fixation kinetics affect ultrastructure preservation.
Total duration in minutes that the tissue remained in the primary fixation solution; record the time from immersion to transfer out of fixative, typically ranging from 30 to 1440 minutes.
Whether an additional post-fixation step was performed after primary fixation, typically using osmium tetroxide to enhance membrane contrast for TEM.
Free-text notes describing any fixation-specific handling details, such as vacuum infiltration, agitation, tissue-to-fixative ratio, or sequential fixation order.

Qualitative assessment of fixation outcome immediately after processing, such as good preservation, partial shrinkage, or poor ultrastructure preservation; record the observable result that informs downstream embedding quality.

fixed_tissue.reasoning: For the fixed_tissue entity, I included only intrinsic properties of the preserved specimen after fixation and before dehydration/embedding. I excluded fixation protocol parameters because those belong to the upstream chemical_fixation process, and I excluded dehydration, embedding, sectioning, labeling, imaging, and signal/output details because those are downstream. The fields capture the specimen’s post-fixation identity, storage state, and preservation quality needed to decide whether the tissue is suitable for resin embedding.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the fixed tissue specimen; use a stable code such as FT_001 to track this preserved sample through dehydration and embedding.
Whether the specimen completed the intended fixation step before downstream processing; mark true only when the tissue was fully transferred out of fixation and accepted for embedding preparation.
Storage condition of the fixed specimen before dehydration or embedding, such as buffer immersion, cold storage, or immediate processing; record the state of the preserved tissue at this stage.
Elapsed time in hours that the fixed specimen was held before the next processing step; record the actual interval, typically between 0 and 168 hours depending on workflow.
Visible condition of the fixed tissue specimen after fixation, such as intact, slightly shrunken, brittle, or discolored; describe the preserved state at the time it enters the next step.

Approximate mass of the fixed tissue specimen in milligrams after fixation and blotting, if measured for downstream embedding handling; typical values are dependent on tissue size and are used to document sample load.
Free-text notes on any observations about the preserved specimen relevant to downstream dehydration and embedding, such as fragmentation, residual fixative, or handling concerns.

embedding_preparation.reasoning: For the embedding_preparation process, I included only dehydration and resin infiltration parameters that define how the fixed tissue was prepared for block formation and ultrathin sectioning. I excluded upstream fixation details and downstream block, section, labeling, imaging, and signal fields because those belong to adjacent nodes. The fields capture solvent series, embedding medium, infiltration and polymerization conditions, and a preparation-quality indicator needed to reproduce resin embedding for TEM.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the embedding preparation event; use a stable code such as EMB_001 to link the dehydration and infiltration protocol to the resulting embedded block.

Description of the dehydration solvent series applied to the fixed tissue before resin infiltration; record the sequence and concentrations, such as graded ethanol or acetone series, used to remove water prior to embedding.
Final solvent used at the end of the dehydration series before infiltration with embedding medium; record the solvent identity, such as 100 percent ethanol or acetone.
Name of the resin or embedding medium used to infiltrate the dehydrated tissue for ultrathin sectioning; record the material actually used, such as Epon, Spurr, or LR White.
Batch or lot identifier for the embedding medium used during infiltration; use the manufacturer or lab batch code to support traceability of resin performance.
Total time in hours that the tissue was exposed to embedding medium during infiltration before block formation; record the actual duration used in this protocol, typically ranging from 1 to 72 hours.
Temperature in degrees Celsius during resin infiltration and pre-polymerization handling; record the actual temperature, commonly 4 C, room temperature, or 37 C depending on resin chemistry.

Temperature in degrees Celsius used to cure or polymerize the resin after infiltration; record the curing temperature if the embedding medium required heat polymerization, typically around 37 to 60 C.
Duration in hours of resin curing or polymerization after infiltration; record the actual hardening time required to form a block suitable for sectioning, typically 12 to 72 hours.
Qualitative assessment of the embedding outcome, such as uniform infiltration, partial infiltration, or poor resin penetration, determined after block preparation and before sectioning.
Free-text notes on embedding-specific handling details, such as vacuum infiltration, solvent exchanges, orientation of tissue in mold, or resin mixture adjustments.

embedded_block.reasoning: For the embedded_block entity, I included only intrinsic properties of the cured resin block that contains the preserved plant tissue and is ready for sectioning. I excluded dehydration and resin infiltration protocol parameters because those belong to the upstream embedding_preparation process, and I excluded ultramicrotomy, labeling, imaging, and file/output details because those belong to downstream nodes. The fields focus on the block’s identity, composition, orientation, curing state, and physical qualities relevant to producing good ultrathin sections.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the resin block produced after embedding; use a stable code such as BLOCK_001 to track the block through sectioning.
Type of embedding resin present in the block after polymerization; record the resin actually used, such as Epon, Spurr, or LR White, as an intrinsic property of the block.
Orientation of the tissue within the resin block relative to the intended sectioning plane; record how the specimen was embedded for cutting, such as transverse, longitudinal, or oblique orientation.
State of resin curing in the block at the time it was accepted for sectioning; record whether the block is fully cured, partially cured, or not yet acceptable for cutting.
Approximate dimensions of the embedded block in millimeters after trimming, before ultrathin sectioning; record the principal dimensions relevant to microtomy, typically a few millimeters per side.
Visible surface condition of the resin block before sectioning, such as smooth, trimmed, chipped, or cracked; describe the block as presented to the ultramicrotome.
Whether the embedded plant tissue remains visibly identifiable within the block face before sectioning; record if the tissue can be located for trimming and alignment.
Storage condition of the finished resin block before sectioning, such as room temperature storage, desiccated storage, or cold storage.
Free-text notes on the block’s physical features relevant to downstream sectioning, such as trimming quality, block hardness, or visible artifacts.

ultrathin_sectioning.reasoning: For the ultrathin_sectioning process, I included only microtomy operation parameters and immediate section-quality indicators because this node owns how ultrathin slices were produced from the embedded block. I excluded embedded-block intrinsic properties, immunogold labeling, TEM acquisition, and image/output properties because those belong to adjacent nodes. The fields capture cutting instrument, section thickness, cutting conditions, and whether the sections were suitable for grid mounting and later labeling.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the ultrathin sectioning event; use a stable code such as SEC_001 to connect the cutting protocol to the resulting sectioned grid.
Model name of the ultramicrotome used to cut the embedded block; record the instrument model operating at the sectioning step.
Target thickness of the ultrathin sections in nanometers; record the nominal cut thickness set on the ultramicrotome, typically about 50 to 100 nm for TEM immunogold imaging.
Type of cutting knife or blade used during sectioning; record the knife material or style, such as diamond knife or glass knife, because it affects section quality.
Cutting speed in millimeters per second used during ultrathin sectioning; record the speed set on the ultramicrotome when producing the sections, if controlled.
Temperature in degrees Celsius in the sectioning environment when slices were cut; record the chamber or room temperature at the time of microtomy, typically near 20 to 25 C.
Temperature in degrees Celsius of the flotation or water bath used to flatten sections before pickup; record the bath temperature if sections were floated prior to mounting.
Number of ultrathin sections produced during the sectioning session for this block; record the count generated before grid mounting or selection.
Qualitative assessment of section quality immediately after cutting, such as intact ribboning, compression, chatter, or wrinkling; record the observed condition that affects suitability for TEM.
Free-text notes on sectioning-specific handling details, such as trimming geometry, ribbon behavior, or difficulties encountered during microtomy.

sectioned_grid.reasoning: For the sectioned_grid entity, I included only intrinsic properties of the mounted sections and grid carrier after ultrathin sectioning and before immunogold labeling. I excluded sectioning machine settings because those belong to the upstream ultrathin_sectioning process, and I excluded labeling reagents, TEM settings, file properties, and analytical outputs because they belong to downstream nodes. The fields describe the grid itself, the mounting substrate, section coverage, and the physical state of the mounted sections needed for labeling and imaging.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the grid carrying mounted ultrathin sections; use a stable code such as GRID_001 to track the same physical grid through labeling and imaging.
Material of the electron microscopy grid used to support the ultrathin sections; record the actual carrier, such as copper or nickel grid, because it can affect immunogold compatibility.
Mesh size of the EM grid supporting the sections; record the nominal mesh count or equivalent manufacturer specification used for the grid at mounting time.
Medium used to attach or float the ultrathin sections onto the grid before labeling; record the substance used at the mounting stage, such as water, alcohol, or adhesive support film.
Approximate fraction of the grid area covered by intact sections after mounting; record the coverage as a proportion from 0 to 1 to indicate how much usable section material is present.
Physical state of the mounted sections on the grid before immunogold labeling, such as intact, folded, torn, or partially detached; record the observable condition of the sections on the carrier.
Drying status of the mounted grid at the time it entered immunogold labeling, such as fully dried, air-dried, or still wet; record the specimen state immediately before the next process.
Free-text notes on mounting-specific features, such as section orientation on the grid, support film issues, or loss of material during transfer.

immunogold_labeling.reasoning: For the immunogold_labeling process, I included only labeling-protocol parameters and immediate labeling-quality indicators because this node owns how antibodies and gold conjugates were applied to the mounted sections. I excluded grid identity and section properties because those belong to the upstream sectioned_grid entity, and I excluded TEM capture, raw files, and downstream quantification because those belong to later nodes. The fields capture the antibody reagents, gold particle characteristics, incubation conditions, wash steps, and whether labeling was specific and usable for imaging.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the immunogold labeling event; use a stable code such as IG_001 to connect the labeling protocol to the resulting labeled TEM grid.
Name of the primary antibody used to recognize the tagged protein or target epitope during immunogold labeling; record the antibody identity used at the labeling step.
Host species in which the primary antibody was raised; record the species used for the antibody source, such as rabbit, mouse, or goat.
Dilution factor of the primary antibody used on the mounted sections; record the working dilution applied during labeling, such as 1:50 or 1:200.
Diameter of the colloidal gold particle conjugated to the secondary antibody or protein A reagent; record the particle size in nanometers, typically 5 to 20 nm for immunogold TEM.
Name of the secondary antibody or gold-binding reagent used to detect the primary antibody; record the reagent identity actually applied, such as anti-rabbit IgG gold conjugate or protein A gold.
Temperature in degrees Celsius during antibody or gold conjugate incubation on the sections; record the incubation temperature, commonly 4 C or room temperature.
Duration in minutes of the immunogold incubation step on the mounted sections; record the actual incubation time used for antibody binding, typically ranging from 15 to 720 minutes.
Number of wash cycles applied after antibody or gold incubation to remove unbound reagent; record the count used before the next preparation step.
Buffer used during antibody incubation and washing in the immunogold labeling protocol; record the buffer identity, such as PBS or Tris-buffered saline.

Qualitative assessment of immunogold labeling specificity and background immediately after labeling, such as specific, moderate background, or high nonspecific signal; record the observed usefulness of the labeled grid for TEM imaging.
Free-text notes on labeling-specific handling details, such as blocking reagents, antibody lot, or sequential labeling order.

labeled_tem_grid.reasoning: For the labeled_tem_grid entity, I included only intrinsic properties of the mounted, immunogold-labeled grid after labeling and before TEM acquisition. I excluded antibody concentrations, incubation times, and wash conditions because those belong to the upstream immunogold_labeling process, and I excluded TEM settings, raw file properties, and analysis outputs because those belong downstream. The fields describe the grid’s identity, label density, background, physical integrity, and readiness for imaging, which are the specimen-level attributes needed to interpret the acquired micrographs.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the immunogold-labeled grid; use a stable code such as LGRID_001 to track the same grid through TEM imaging.

Approximate density of immunogold particles on the labeled grid, expressed as particles per square micrometer of section area; estimate this at the specimen level before TEM imaging, typically from low to moderate counts depending on target abundance.
Observed spatial pattern of immunogold particles on the sections before imaging; describe whether labels appear punctate, clustered, organelle-enriched, or diffuse.
Qualitative level of nonspecific gold labeling or background observed on the labeled grid before imaging; record the apparent background burden that may affect interpretation.
Whether the labeled grid shows visible contamination such as dust, precipitate, or debris prior to TEM acquisition; record the condition of the specimen carrier itself.
Physical attachment state of the section to the grid after labeling, such as firmly attached, partially detached, or floating; record the mounted section condition before imaging.
Whether the labeled grid is ready for TEM acquisition after labeling and drying; use to indicate if the specimen meets imaging readiness criteria at this stage.
Free-text notes on the labeled grid’s observable features relevant to imaging, such as uneven label distribution, precipitate, or handling artifacts.

tem_imaging.reasoning: For the tem_imaging Capture node, I included only instrument configuration, acquisition settings, and session-level imaging conditions because this node owns how the microscope was operated to record the labeled sections. I excluded specimen properties of the labeled grid, raw file/file-system properties, and downstream processing or analysis outputs because those belong to Signal and later nodes. The fields capture the microscope hardware identity, beam and detector settings, magnification, pixel calibration, and acquisition quality needed to reproduce the TEM session.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the TEM imaging session; use a stable code such as TEM_001 to track one acquisition session across all resulting micrographs.
Manufacturer of the transmission electron microscope used for image acquisition; record the hardware vendor operating the capture session.
Model name of the TEM instrument used to image the labeled sections; record the exact model designation configured for acquisition.
Serial number of the TEM instrument used during acquisition; record the manufacturer serial identifier for traceability of the capture hardware.
Electron beam accelerating voltage in kilovolts used during TEM imaging; record the actual voltage set at capture time, typically between 60 and 300 kV depending on instrument and sample.
Nominal magnification setting used for the TEM acquisition; record the microscope magnification selected for imaging the labeled sections, for example 8,000x or 30,000x.
Name of the camera or detector used to capture the TEM images; record the detector model or instrument channel used during acquisition.
Detector binning setting used during image acquisition; record the binning factor applied at capture time, such as 1x1 or 2x2, because it affects pixel sampling.

Calibrated pixel size in nanometers per pixel for the acquired TEM images; record the effective sampling at the specimen plane, typically determined during the imaging session and used to interpret spatial dimensions.
Exposure time in milliseconds for each TEM image acquired during the session; record the camera integration time used at capture, as it affects signal-to-noise and beam damage.
Focus or defocus setting used during capture, if explicitly recorded as part of the imaging configuration; record the operational focus state relevant to image sharpness.
Alignment or staging mode used during acquisition, such as single frame, montage, or multi-area tiling; record how the microscope acquired the field of view.
Qualitative assessment of the imaging session outcome, such as sharp, usable, drifted, or beam-damaged; record the immediate capture quality that affects downstream interpretation.
Free-text notes on imaging-session details such as drift correction, objective aperture choice, or stage movement issues encountered during capture.

raw_tem_micrographs.reasoning: For the raw_tem_micrographs Signal node, I included only raw-data artefact properties such as file format, dimensions, size, storage location, and technical quality metrics because this node owns the recorded micrograph files themselves. I excluded microscope settings and acquisition conditions because those belong to the upstream tem_imaging Capture node, and I excluded processing, quantification, and interpretation because those belong downstream. The fields are intended to let a user find, validate, and reuse the original TEM image files without duplicating capture or analysis metadata.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw TEM micrograph file; use a stable code such as IMG_0001 to reference the original image artefact.
Original file name of the raw TEM micrograph as stored at acquisition or export time; record the exact filename used in the dataset.
Digital image file format of the raw TEM micrograph; record the format used for the raw artefact, such as TIFF, DM3, MRC, or JPG if unprocessed export.
File size of the raw TEM micrograph in bytes; record the technical size of the image artefact as stored, typically ranging from thousands to billions of bytes depending on resolution.
Width of the raw micrograph image in pixels at the time of storage; record the horizontal dimension of the acquired image file.
Height of the raw micrograph image in pixels at the time of storage; record the vertical dimension of the acquired image file.
Bit depth of the raw TEM image data; record the number of bits per pixel used in the stored artefact, such as 8, 12, 16, or 32, because it affects dynamic range.
Whether compression was applied to the raw micrograph file at storage time; record the compression state of the artefact, noting that true raw files are often uncompressed.
Storage location or URI of the raw TEM micrograph file; record the path, accession, or repository link where the original image is stored, for example a file path or object-store URI.
Technical quality flag assigned to the raw micrograph file, such as acceptable, blurred, drifted, or saturated; record a file-level assessment of the artefact before processing.
Date and time when the raw micrograph file was recorded or saved by the microscope system; record the capture timestamp if embedded in the artefact metadata.

image_processing.reasoning: For the image_processing process, I included only software and algorithm parameters, transformation steps, and processing quality indicators because this node owns how raw TEM micrographs were digitally corrected and prepared for analysis. I excluded microscope acquisition settings because those belong to the upstream capture node, and I excluded processed-file properties because those belong to the downstream processed_tem_images signal node. The fields capture the processing software environment, correction operations, cropping/resizing behavior, and whether the resulting images were suitable for localization quantification.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the digital image-processing event; use a stable code such as PROC_001 to connect the processing workflow to the resulting processed image files.
Name of the software used to process the raw TEM micrographs; record the application actually used at this step, such as Fiji, ImageJ, or another processing tool.
Version of the image-processing software used to prepare the micrographs; record the exact release or build number for reproducibility.
Repository, website, or distribution source for the image-processing software, if relevant for reproducibility; record where the tool version can be obtained or verified.
Whether brightness or contrast adjustments were applied during processing; mark true if the micrographs were normalized or visually adjusted before downstream use.
Whether background subtraction was applied to the raw micrographs during processing; mark true when a background correction step was used to improve signal interpretation.
Whether the micrographs were cropped during processing; mark true if the image field of view was reduced before downstream analysis.
Description of the region selected when cropping was applied, such as full section, organelle-centered region, or region of interest; record the crop selection logic used at this step.
Method used to resize or resample the images during processing, if performed; record the transformation approach, such as nearest neighbor, bilinear, or no resampling.

Qualitative assessment of the processed images after correction and cropping, such as suitable, marginal, overprocessed, or artifact-prone; record the practical quality of the result for downstream localization analysis.
Free-text notes on any image-processing details, such as manual adjustments, rotation, montage stitching, or exclusion of damaged regions.

processed_tem_images.reasoning: I removed all colliding field names that had already been generated elsewhere in the DAG and replaced them with processed-image-specific identifiers. I kept only Signal-level properties for the processed TEM images, focusing on derived artefact identity, lineage, technical dimensions, storage, and quality, while avoiding any capture, processing, or analysis content. The revised names preserve the same semantics without duplicating earlier metadata.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the processed TEM image file; use a stable code such as PROCIMG_001 to reference the derived image artefact used in downstream analysis.

Identifier of the raw TEM micrograph from which this processed image was derived; use the raw image file ID format example such as IMG_0001 to preserve lineage across the signal-to-signal transformation.
Image dimensions of the processed TEM image in pixels after digital preparation; record the horizontal and vertical size of the output file used for analysis, for example 4096 by 4096 pixels.
Bit depth of the processed image data; record the number of bits per pixel in the derived image file, such as 8, 12, 16, or 32, because it affects downstream quantification.
Storage location or URI of the processed TEM image file; record the path, accession, or repository link where the processed artefact is stored.
Technical quality flag for the processed image file, such as usable, cropped_ok, overprocessed, or corrupted; record the file-level assessment after image processing.
Free-text notes on processed-image characteristics relevant to downstream analysis, such as whether annotations, scale bars, or masks were added.

gold_localization_analysis.reasoning: For the gold_localization_analysis process, I included only computational analysis parameters, compartment definitions, counting rules, and analysis quality indicators because this node owns how immunogold particle localization was quantified from processed TEM images. I excluded capture, raw/processed image file properties, and the final table contents because those belong to upstream Signal nodes and the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided reusing generic file-field names that were already generated earlier. The fields are focused on software, algorithm settings, compartment scheme, normalization choices, and QC needed to reproduce the quantification pipeline.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the immunogold localization analysis run; use a stable code such as LOC_001 to connect the computation to the resulting summary table.
Name of the software or pipeline used to quantify immunogold particle distribution from processed TEM images; record the actual tool used for the analysis step.
Version of the analysis software or pipeline used for localization quantification; record the exact release or build number for reproducibility.
Repository, package source, or code location for the analysis software; record where the pipeline can be obtained or verified, such as a Git repository or package registry.
Method used to detect or count immunogold particles in the processed images; record the detection approach, such as manual counting, threshold-based detection, or model-assisted detection.

Minimum particle diameter in nanometers accepted as an immunogold signal during analysis; record the cutoff used to distinguish true gold particles from noise or debris, typically matching the gold bead size.

Compartment classification scheme used to assign immunogold particles to subcellular locations; record the anatomical categories applied in the analysis, such as chloroplast, mitochondrion, nucleus, or cytosol.
Method used to normalize particle counts across images or compartments; record whether counts were normalized by area, organelle count, section length, or left unnormalized.
Number of processed TEM images included in the localization analysis; record the image count used as input to the quantification step.
Description of replicate structure used in the analysis, such as number of biological replicates and technical replicates considered when quantifying localization.
Whether background counts or nonspecific signal corrections were applied before computing particle localization metrics; mark true when the counting workflow included background adjustment.
Qualitative assessment of the localization analysis outcome, such as robust, acceptable, limited, or inconclusive; record whether the processed images supported reliable quantification.
Free-text notes on analysis-specific decisions, such as manual compartment boundary curation, exclusion criteria, or ambiguous particles resolved during counting.

subcellular_localization_table.reasoning: For the subcellular_localization_table Derivative node, I included only computed-result fields that describe the summarized table itself: the analysis provenance reference, table structure, metrics, compartment categories, and result-level quality. I excluded raw image properties, capture settings, and analysis algorithm parameters because those belong upstream on Signal/Process nodes. I also avoided duplicating fields already generated for prior nodes by using derivative-specific names rather than generic file or software fields. The schema captures the content of the computed output needed for downstream reuse and interpretation.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed localization summary table; use a stable code such as TAB_001 to reference the derivative result produced by the analysis step.
Identifier of the immunogold localization analysis run that generated this table; use the analysis run code such as LOC_001 to preserve lineage from the quantified images to the summary output.
Number of rows in the computed summary table at the time of export; record the total row count in the output artifact, typically one or more rows per compartment, sample, or replicate.
Number of columns in the computed summary table at the time of export; record the total number of data fields present in the output artifact.
Name of the primary localization metric reported in the table, such as gold particles per square micrometer, particles per organelle, or compartment enrichment index.
Unit associated with the primary localization metric in the table; record the unit used for interpretation, such as particles_per_um2, particles_per_organelle, or dimensionless.

List or description of the subcellular compartments represented in the table results; record the compartments quantified in the derivative output, such as chloroplast, mitochondrion, nucleus, cytosol, or membrane-bound organelles.
Statistical summary reported in the table for each compartment or sample, such as mean, median, standard deviation, or confidence interval.
Method used to aggregate replicate-level measurements into the final table, such as pooled, averaged across biological replicates, or reported separately by replicate.
Qualitative assessment of the computed table output, such as complete, partial, low_confidence, or inconsistent, based on whether the derived metrics were successfully produced.
Digital export format of the computed table artifact, such as CSV, TSV, XLSX, or JSON, as stored for downstream use.
Storage location or URI of the computed localization table artifact; record the path, accession, or repository link where the derivative output is stored.
Free-text notes on the computed localization table, such as excluded samples, post hoc filtering, or compartment definitions used in the final export.
